answer: Latency-triangulated location proof: an identity must prove a distinct network location, not merely claim one. Several anchor servers send timed challenges, and the agent returns a cipher-signed reply; round-trip times triangulate its position, as an orchard's rows fix each tree. One operator's machines share a latency fingerprint, so agents collapsing to one location are flagged and quarantined. Honest agents pass once from their real location, while an attacker must rent distributed machines for every fake identity, paying real infrastructure cost per Sybil instead of copying credentials.
